title: Plan B
dateline: The morning after the fish-market raid.
mood: A drone back on its charger, a nap in class, and a plan for coming home, said on a roof just in case.

hero.alt: In a bright Academy stairwell a blonde student in uniform swings down the hall with her arms flung wide and a silver dragon machine at her side, streamers of light swirling around her, while pink-haired Guinevere and black-haired Vexana follow a few steps behind on the stairs.

segs.t: Guinevere woke with the phone still on her pillow and her taped wrist under her cheek. She had fallen asleep counting.
Gray light came through the gap of her door. On the shelf, two rings glowed on the drone charger.
She sat up. The cradle that had been empty last night was full. Her lost drone sat in it, its yellow ring lit. Both ears stood up.
She had not heard a step. She always heard steps.
Guinevere held out her hand. The drone lifted off the charger and came to it, and held its height.
She knew only one person who straightened brackets with two fingers.
She went to the door in her socks, the drone at her shoulder.
Down the corridor, Vexana stood at the window in her running things, a tactics book open in her hands. She turned a page as if she had been there for hours.
“You took it,” said Guinevere.
“It was in a gutter,” said Vexana. “Now it isn’t.”
“It was on my charger.”
“Your door was open.”
Guinevere had a word ready about crosswinds. She looked at the drone, and kept it to herself.
She lifted her chin instead. “That fall yesterday. It was a lady’s refinement.”
“Four,” said Vexana.
“Three. A lady stands on three.”
“Four.” Vexana shut the book. “I counted.”
At the House, Hester had counted three at every fall, however long Guinevere took to get up. Vexana counted what it really took, and said it to her face.
Guinevere laughed out loud in the empty corridor. She ran back for her shoes.
They ran at first light. The drone came all the way round the grounds at her shoulder and never once sank.
Selrick Academy, the hall. The week the newcomers became Aspirants.
Guinevere stood along the wall in her uniform and watched the girl with the scythe.
Ruby held it point-down on the floor in front of Lesley. Guinevere had seen her hold it like that before, on dirt.

Weeks had gone since the fish market. The day the black ships landed, she and Vexana had held the giants’ front beside Lesley’s squads until dark. Days later the gate portal dropped them at a cleared lot by the dome’s foot. Guinevere stood at the end of the soldiers’ line with her drones up, and Vexana beside her with her staff.
A black ship settled on the dirt. Two girls came down its ramp. The one with the scythe planted it and bowed.
Guinevere knew that bow. A manners tutor had spent years on hers. Then the girl called herself an heir, and Guinevere nearly laughed.
Another one.
Now Lesley was on the last words of her speech. By the door Vexana waited with her arms folded, and Guinevere was waving at her with her whole arm.
The speech ended. In front, Layla turned around and looked straight at her.
Guinevere did not stop. She swung the same wave at Layla.
For a second Layla only looked. Then she lifted two fingers, once.
Two fingers,
thought Guinevere.
From Layla, that’s a parade.
The hall emptied. On her way past the door, Guinevere caught a fistful of Vexana’s sleeve and kept walking. Vexana came along behind her, out of the hall and into the light.
The third-year classroom. Days later.
Guinevere had a desk in the second row, and Vexana the one beside it. Every desk had its own glass screen, lit faintly from underneath.
The lesson had begun when the door slid open. Selena, the blonde girl from the Science Division, came in with a lollipop in her cheek. Silverbolt, her dragon-shaped machine, clicked in at her heel.
“Selena,” said the teacher. “Late again.”
“My guardian already called it in.”
The teacher checked a tablet and sighed. The note was there.
Selena dropped into her desk in the front row and laid her head on her arms.
“I’m taking a little nap. You all just keep going.”
The teacher looked at the sleeping head and went on with the lesson.
A paper plane crossed the room and hit Selena on the head. Every face turned to Layla. She was copying the board with great care. The teacher had not written a word on it yet.
“Mmm... just five more minutes...”
Then Selena sat up, wide awake. “There was a cupcake,” she told the room. “It was mine.”

blocks.caption: A nap, a paper plane, and a cupcake that was hers.

media.alt: In a bright classroom Selena sleeps on her arms at her desk, dreaming of a cupcake with a cherry on top, while a classmate behind her holds up a paper plane.

segs.t: She spread her fingers over her desk. A suit of armor rose out of the screen and turned slowly in the air. It had a visor, and a weapon along one arm. A label under it read ENDER MECHA SUIT.
“Ender plating, my own design.”
At the next desk, Fanny leaned in to look at the joints. Her face lit up. “Those joints would take a hit.”
Angela came across the room with her doll in the crook of her arm. She stood very still in front of the suit and said nothing.
Ruby leaned forward from her seat by the wall, one row behind Selena. “Does it come in my size?”
“Everything does,” said Selena. “For a price.”
Guinevere studied the suit. It was good. She decided to find the fault later.
Beside her, Vexana watched the plates turn until Selena closed her hand on them.
Afterward Selena went down the stairs with Silverbolt clicking beside her. Guinevere and Vexana came a few steps behind. A boy leaned over the rail.
“Selena! The things in your head. Dangerous!”
He meant it as praise. Selena waved her lollipop over her shoulder without turning.
“One day, when the haze clears, you’ll come to know the real me.”
The whole stairwell laughed. Guinevere laughed loudest, her head thrown back.

That afternoon they climbed to the dormitory roof. Washing flapped on the lines. Guinevere sat on the green rail and swung her boots over the drop. Vexana sat with her back against it, a page folded small in her fingers.
“I read Chang’e’s paper,” said Vexana. “The one on black holes.”
The boots stopped. “The one she wouldn’t tell me about? When?”
“The day of the tree. I should have said.”
“The day of the tree? That was last year!”
“Yes.”
“You went to the library without me?”
“You would have talked.”
“I would not have talked!” Guinevere glared down at the top of the black head.
She’s carried that since the tree. Next to me, the whole time.
“Fine.” It came out smaller than she meant. “What does it say?”
Vexana did not unfold the page. She knew it by heart.
“A black hole tears apart whatever falls in. The body first.”
“Lovely.”
“Then one line. ‘An Aspirant’s light would shine on inside a black hole, and find its way home.’”
“Chang’e said nobody’s ever seen anything come back out,” said Guinevere. “Not even light. She said it in front of the whole class.”
“Nobody has seen it. The paper says an Aspirant is different.”
“Different how?”
“Not the body. The part of you that thinks and hopes.” Vexana’s thumb pressed the folded page. “It would keep shining in there. It would pierce its way out and come back to the human world.”
“How would she know?”
“She sealed a lit core in a glass chamber and pumped out the air. Every needle on her dials fell to nothing. The light held.”
Guinevere frowned at the sky. “So our light doesn’t need air.”
“She thinks it needs nothing around it at all.”
Vexana’s fingertip went to the small gold star at her collar. It brightened under her touch. At Guinevere’s collar the other star brightened with it.
“The paper never says two,” said Vexana. “But I think two would shine brighter.”
Guinevere sat very still for a moment. Then she slapped the rail. “So we can’t get near the void. Fine! At least we know the way back out of it.”
“It’s untested. The paper says would, not will.”
Guinevere stabbed a finger at the sky. “Plan A, I smash the Core and we win. Plan B, we come home. Say it.”
“No.”
“Say ‘Plan B.’”
Vexana looked down at the page. “Plan B.”
“Two of us, shining out of the dark and home!” Guinevere sang it in her ceremony voice, badly. “I’ll never forget it. You’ve given me a song.”
“Stop that.”
She sang it twice more to the washing lines. Then she propped her chin on her fist.
“Why tell me now?”
Vexana folded the page into a smaller square. “In case.”
“In case of what?”
“In case.”
A siren cut across the roof. Guinevere was on her feet before the first note ended. She caught Vexana’s hand and hauled her up.
“Plan A first.”
